seoTitle: 👉 Backhand Index Pointing Right Emoji Meaning
seoDescription: Learn what the Backhand Index Pointing Right emoji 👉 really means.

longForm.overview:
The 👉 Backhand Index Pointing Right emoji was added in Unicode 6 (2010) and is drawn as a yellow hand with the back of the hand showing and the index finger pointing to the right. The visual cue reads instantly as 'look at this,' direction, or the visible 'check this out' tag. By 2026 👉 has become the go-to emoji for the attention-directing tag, the visible 'over there' default, and the layered-combination-default for shy-pointing-coded combos like 👉👈.

In modern chat 👉 does very specific work. People send it as a literal direction tag, as the visible 'look at this' marker, or as the shy-pointing-and-combining base. The pointing-backhand-index-finger is the visual cue that the message is directing attention. Writers should pick 👉 when the read is directing attention or coding the pointer in a combination, and avoid it when the read is different — ☝️ fits better for literal up-pointing.
longForm.howPeopleUseIt:
👉 lands on a friend's 'check this out' message, in a work channel where someone is directing attention, and in a dating-app DM where the sender is referencing a previous message. The pointing-backhand-index-finger anchors the read.

In close-friends chats 👉 reads as the universal 'look here' tag and the pointing-backhand default. On X the emoji punctuates 'this thread' coded tweets. The emoji pairs with 👈 for the layered shy-pointing combo and with 👇 for the layered down-pointing pair.
longForm.whenNotToUse: Skip 👉 in any context where the direction is up — ☝️ fits better. Avoid 👉 in ironic contexts where the pointing is faked — 🙄 fits better when the attention-directing is performed.
longForm.howToReply:
If a friend sends 👉 on an attention-directing message, mirror with a sentence that engages what they pointed to. The pointing chain needs an audience.

If 👉 lands as the shy-pointing base of a combo, reply with another 👉 or 👈. And if you want to send 👉 yourself, pair it with the subject so the direction is clear.

faqs.question: What does 👉 mean in text?
faqs.answer: 👉 means 'look at this,' 'over there,' or attention-direction. The pointing-backhand-index-finger is the visual cue that the message is directing attention.

faqs.question: What does 👉 mean with 👈?
faqs.answer: 👉👈 is the shy-pointing combo: the sender is doing the visible 'I am being shy about asking' coded request, usually for something they want.

faqs.question: Is 👉 flirty?
faqs.answer: Sometimes. 👉 by itself is neutral. In a combo like 👉👈 or paired with shy-coded content, it reads as flirty-coded 'I am being shy about this.'

faqs.question: What does 👉 mean at work?
faqs.answer: In Slack, 👉 reads as the 'check this thread' tag. Pair with a sentence about the message so the channel stays useful.
